time="0.8s" /> Into the main street of Yellow Sky. <break time="0.8s" /> His boots had red tops. <break time="0.8s" /> With gilded imps on them. <break time="0.8s" /> The kind beloved in winter. <break time="0.8s" /> By little sledding boys. <break time="0.8s" /> On the hillsides of New England. <break time="0.8s" /> He held a long, heavy, blue black revolver. <break time="0.8s" /> In each hand. <break time="0.8s" /> And he often yelled. <break time="0.8s" /> And these cries rang through a village. <break time="0.8s" /> That seemed to be deserted. <break time="0.8s" /> The calm adobe houses. <break time="0.8s" /> Preserved their dignity. <break time="0.8s" /> And there was no offer of fight. <break time="0.8s" /> No offer of anything. <break time="0.8s" /> And the man called angrily to the sky. <break time="0.8s" /> When the bartenders dog walked away growling. <break time="0.8s" /> Scratchy fired at the ground. <break time="0.8s" /> Just in front of it. <break time="0.8s" /> And the frightened animal galloped away in terror. <break time="0.8s" /> Remembering Jack Potter. <break time="0.8s" /> His ancient antagonist. <break time="0.8s" /> He concluded. <break time="0.8s" /> That it would be a glad thing. <break time="0.8s" /> To go to Potters house. <break time="0.8s" /> And make him come out and fight. <break time="0.8s" /> Potters house presented the same still front. <break time="0.8s" /> As the other houses. <break time="0.8s" /> And when Scratchy howled a challenge. <break time="0.8s" /> It regarded him. <break time="0.8s" /> As might a great stone god. <break time="0.8s" /> He churned himself into deepest rage. <break time="0.8s" /> Over the stillness of the house. <break time="0.8s" /> Fuming at it. <break time="0.8s" /> As the winter wind attacks a prairie cabin.
